summary: This article explains why cities plan parks and green spaces, how they improve air quality, lower temperatures, and support residents' wellbeing, and examples of green-space projects in Saudi cities like Riyadh and Jeddah.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Urban Green Spaces and City Parks” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: relating to a city or a densely built-up area
harmful substances, such as smoke or trash, that damage air, water, or land
a gas in the air that people and animals need to breathe

challengeTerms.def: the variety of different plants, animals, and other living things in an area
able to continue for a long time without causing lasting harm to the environment
the basic structures and systems, such as roads, parks, and buildings, that a city needs to function

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that cities should build more parks and green spaces, even if it costs a lot of money? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain two different benefits that parks give to a city, and describe a detail from the article that supports each benefit.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review urban, pollution, and oxygen, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses biodiversity, sustainable, and infrastructure to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
